clue.text: A substance consumed by male, rather naughty in legal office

indicators.note: what is consumed by the male goes straight after him, so the next pieces follow the male's letter

parts.note: taken as written
the gist of something is its substance or essence
racy describes something mildly risque, rather naughty

explanation.surface: A magistrate's office is scandalised when a man is caught with something illicit and rather risque.
explanation.definitionFit: Magistracy is the office or post held by a magistrate, a role in the legal system.

clue.text: Nobody's wife is a failure?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the title for a woman married to no one
second meaning: a shot or attempt that does not hit

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites reading 'Nobody' as a name; it simply means an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is the title for an unmarried woman, and a miss is also an unsuccessful attempt.

clue.text: Heavyweight fighter needing a light arranged over ring

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer needs the ring lights set up before the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: Goliath was the Philistine giant felled by David.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath is the biblical giant warrior, a byword for a huge champion.

clue.text: Fair acting in play represented in prim snapshots

indicators.note: represented means shown in another form, so these letters are recast

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fair acting in a stage play is captured in rather formal photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportsmanship is behaving fairly and honourably while taking part in a game.

clue.text: Right clue finally leading to wrong answer

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word clue

parts.note: its last letter is used
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Getting the last part of a crossword clue right still leads to a wrong solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp reply, a quick answer to a remark.

clue.text: Failure of nerve due to lack of adequate hose?

definitions.meaning: the real meaning: losing courage before a big step

definitions.text: due to lack of adequate hose
definitions.meaning: the joke reading: without decent socks or stockings, your toes would feel chilly

explanation.walkthrough: Hose here means stockings, not a garden hose; the literal reading is chilly toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting cold feet is the idiom for losing courage before doing something planned.

clue.text: Substitute put in for striker, as result of injury

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a worker brought in to replace one on strike
second meaning: the crust that forms over a healing wound

explanation.walkthrough: The football picture of a substitute for a striker hides the industrial-dispute sense of strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a strikebreaker, and also the dried crust over a healing cut.

clue.text: Caught, then appearing versus court, one gets put inside

definitions.text: Caught, then appearing versus court, one gets put inside

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
on, as a performer is on when appearing on stage
the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone arrested, then tried in court, ends up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue tells the criminal's story while also building the word; the numeral for one goes just ahead of the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict is a person found guilty and sent to prison.

clue.text: Women entitled to give piece of music zero points

parts.note: a bar is a short measured section of music
a ness is a headland or point of land, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Female judges are allowed to give a musical performance nul points.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness is a coastal headland, common in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronesses are women holding a noble title, so they are titled ladies.

clue.text: Dramatic success for act of betrayal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a show for which every ticket is bought
second meaning: abandoning principles or allies for gain

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses of the same compound noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-out is a show playing to full houses, and also a treacherous compromise.

clue.text: Member of class left good source of income

parts.note: a nice little earner is something that brings in money

explanation.surface: A pupil leaves school for a lucrative job.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is a pupil or student, one of those taught together in a class.

clue.text: Non-committal type, awfully obstinate, isn't changing

indicators.note: done awfully, so the letters come out jumbled
changing order, so these letters too are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fence-sitter is dreadfully stubborn and won't budge.
explanation.walkthrough: OBSTINATE gives ABSTENTIO and ISNT gives NIST, each rearranged in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstentionist declines to vote or take sides, refusing to commit either way.

clue.text: Following a trend, in a way

parts.note: after means following in time or order
taken as written
a fashion is a current trend or vogue

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up with what's in vogue, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about following trends; the definition is just the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to some extent, in a rough or imperfect manner.

clue.text: Wrong on estimate for accommodation

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A builder's quote for housing turns out to be wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a small flat on two floors, a type of dwelling.

clue.text: In hospital, immersed in a large volume

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: immersed in means the hospital letter is sunk inside the other words

parts.note: a tome is a big, heavy book

explanation.surface: A patient in hospital is absorbed in reading a huge book.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at home means being in, present in one's house rather than out.

clue.text: They remind some men to saw a couple of bits off each end

indicators.text: a couple of bits off each end
indicators.note: trimming two letters from the front and two from the back of the phrase leaves the rest

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some workmen are told to saw two pieces off each end of a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: Mementos are keepsakes that bring back memories of people or events.

clue.text: Bound over unnamed adolescent, one who has been expelled

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: roped means tied up, bound

indicators.note: unnamed means the abbreviation for named is removed

parts.note: a teen is a teenager

explanation.surface: A court binds over an anonymous youth, who is then thrown out of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: To be bound over is a British court order to keep the peace; here it is wordplay. N is an abbreviation for name or named.
explanation.definitionFit: A deportee is a person forcibly sent out of a country.

clue.text: Source of support for Edward II

parts.note: the numeral two marks the second of a line
ER, Edward Rex, the royal cipher of a King Edward

explanation.surface: Someone asks who backed the medieval king Edward the Second.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Rex as well as Regina: Edward VII's cipher was ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A seconder backs a proposal formally at a meeting, a source of support.

clue.text: Exclusive groups have measured intelligence in things like this

indicators.note: in places the intelligence measure within the other word

parts.note: the clue refers to itself: this is one of the clues
IQ, intelligence quotient

explanation.surface: Elite circles test their members' intelligence with riddles of this kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Things like this' points at the clue you are reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliques are small, closed social circles that exclude outsiders.

clue.text: Butt of jokes is too gentlemanly, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the phrase is used, the run of letters sitting inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man teased by others is simply too polite to object.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a comic's foil, the one on the receiving end of the joke.

clue.text: Person who's experienced untold handicaps, in part

indicators.note: in part means the letters are found as a portion of the following words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran has lived through countless disadvantages.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is a veteran who has long practice at something.

clue.text: Belter given new arrangement for top singer

indicators.note: a new arrangement of the letters is a reordering of them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A loud singer's song gets a fresh orchestration for a star vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' means highest in pitch, not best.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy singer with the highest voice part in a choir.

clue.text: Noise from horse initially blows cover for us in vicinity

parts.note: a horse neighs

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word blows

parts.note: its first letter is used
our is the possessive belonging to us
a hood covers the head

explanation.surface: A horse whinnies and snorts beneath a blanket somewhere nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbourhood is the surrounding area or district, the vicinity.

clue.text: Diplomat with no love for green cause

indicators.note: with no means the letter for love is dropped from the word

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic messenger
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: An unloved diplomat takes up an environmental campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Envy is what makes one green, as in green with envy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy is the cause of being green with envy.

clue.text: The drum he'd taken out, favourite instrument

indicators.note: taken out means those letters are removed from the words before them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A band member removed the drum he liked, leaving another instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet is a brass musical instrument.

clue.text: It is where you think, this country?

indicators.note: the word It is located in the organ of thought, so it sits inside it

parts.note: the brain is what you think with
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about where you would really place this nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is the country of the Sunday Telegraph's readership, the one 'this' points at.

clue.text: Conclusions reached in the media, perhaps, overly simple

indicators.note: the conclusions of words are their final letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The press, it is suggested, reaches judgements that are too simplistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overly' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means not difficult, straightforward.

clue.text: You'll find it thus in hospitality suite

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: the word it appears in this manner
the letters i-t turn up three times in these two words

explanation.walkthrough: Look at the letters: hospITalITy suITe contains 'it' again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeatedly means over and over, many times, as the two letters recur here.
